about.title: About Us
about.desc: Formax Racing Team was founded in October 2009. We built the first FSC race car in Guangdong Province and were among the earliest initiators of the FSC competition. Founded by a group of passionate university students, our team comprises undergraduates from mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, business administration, and other disciplines. We are a university-level research team co-supported by South China University of Technology and its School of Mechanical and Automotive Engineering. With strong backing from the university, the school, and society, we independently design and build two brand-new Formula Student cars each year, competing in the Formula Student Electric China (FSEC) and Formula Student Autonomous China (FSAC). Our mission is to cultivate innovative talent through hands-on engineering practice. 'Dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence' is our motto. Together with our race cars, we continuously push technical limits, achieve outstanding results in competitions, and accumulate invaluable practical experience. Over sixteen years, from combustion to electric to autonomous, the team has witnessed countless youthful journeys. Time passes swiftly, washing away the traces of history, but the sweat engraved in our honors is remembered by all.

AF24.story: A-Future24 is the fifth-generation driverless Formula Student race car we developed over 12 months. This is a pioneering vehicle. From concept design to final testing, the entire team invested over 5,000 hours of work. As our team's first driverless car featuring a carbon fiber monocoque and dual AMK in-wheel motors, we faced unprecedented challenges during design and manufacturing. Through countless simulations and tests, working day and night, we ultimately developed this stable and precise driverless race car. The most unforgettable moment was during the final high-speed track drive event, when we persevered through sudden heavy rain with team members taking shifts to ensure every system was at its best. Torrential rain could not dampen our passion, and after the storm came the moonlight. This spirit of 'dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence' allowed us to defend our national third-place title at the 2024 Formula Student China competition, preserving the A03 car number for the next generation of driverless race cars. Season 24 has concluded; we will forge ahead in Season 25.

AF25.story:
A-Future25 is our sixth-generation driverless formula car, twelve months in the making. As the team’s second driverless car with a carbon monocoque and dual AMK in-wheel motors, we put the emphasis on the autonomous system. Through countless simulations and tests, working late into the night, we finally produced a stable and precise driverless race car.

Yet when we walked confidently into the dynamic events, the car on the track was not the car we had practised with.

In the figure-eight the INS drifted strangely and we fell back on offset parameters we had never used before. In the acceleration run we ran into RES interference we had never seen, and AS Ready kept slipping away; on the last — and only — successful run, a Ready timeout meant it did not count.

The one chance to turn the season around was the high-speed tracking event at the end.

Our perception held up under the pressure and completed the mapping lap perfectly. But on the second lap the car began to weave, and we knew at once that it was a control problem. We tuned frantically, and then the problems came one after another — a stop distance we had forgotten to change, a speed profile that suddenly failed… none of which had ever appeared in practice. The clock ran on, and after one slow, safe completion lap we knew there was probably no time to try again.

For everyone there, it was a heavy day. Before it, we had imagined AF25 flying around the track a thousand times; we had not imagined these few hours turning out this way. Compared with the electric car that finished its endurance, what was left here was more red-eyed bitter smiling, more heads held in hands, more bitten lips and self-reproach.

Even with everyone’s eyes red, we still took a national first prize at the 2025 Formula Student China and secured the number A04 for the next driverless car. For Auto-Future, an unsatisfying 2025 season is over. For 2026, we go again.

EF25.story: E-Future24 was the eleventh-generation electric Formula Student race car we developed over 12 months. In Season 23, we designed the team's first-ever four-motor race car, but it dramatically failed just 100 meters before the endurance finish line, unable to complete the race. In Season 24, we quickly passed all static inspections, but due to some design flaws, we couldn't push the car to its true limits before the endurance events, and we encountered unexpected issues during the static presentation. Then came Season 25. EF25, or as we prefer to call it, EF24B — born out of both budget constraints and the unresolved feelings from the EF24 competition, it was the answer our teammates delivered for their dream EF24. It features a redesigned aerodynamics package, repositioned front suspension, optimized TVC algorithm... every innovation crystallizes the lessons learned by teammates during the Season 24 competition. Through various challenges, our EF-25 raced on the track. EF-25 attracted attention from many rival teams due to its extremely high level of completion. We also gained recognition from judges during the static presentation, advancing to the design finals and securing fourth place, along with the Outstanding Aerodynamics Award. During static inspection, almost all items passed on the first attempt. On the dynamic track, this race car did not disappoint our teammates — it claimed fifth place in the Autocross event, earned a Top starting position, and ultimately took third place nationwide in the endurance event. At the moment the car crossed the finish line and passed re-inspection, teammates embraced each other, tears streaming down, sharing the hardships of the past year. Our motto thundered from the podium: 'Dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence!' Amidst joy and regret, our Season 25 concluded with a National First Prize. The story of Season 25 has drawn to a close; we are gearing up for Season 26!

EF26.story:
E-Future26 is our twelfth-generation electric formula car, a full year in the making.

In the 2025 season we scored the best result of our four-motor era — fourth overall nationally — and with it earned E-Future26 the number E04. Yet last year’s E-Future25, hero though she was, was also a veteran: we would rather call her EF24B. Her layout and electrical platform descend straight from EF24 — a rear-biased centre of gravity, an oversized yaw inertia, and the flaw the four-motor era has carried since its very first year: too much mass. Keep that platform and our dynamic results could never take another step forward.

So E-Future26 made exactly those the first priorities: a low-inertia layout, a compact electrical architecture…

After fighting through a shortage of funding and a monocoque mould that would not cooperate, EF26 emerged. Her design caught up with the thinking of China’s top four-motor teams; the overweight body we had been criticised for was gone — 233 kg, Formax’s first step toward lighter, faster, stronger. The judges recognised it too: we reached the design final again and took fourth place. Two finals in a row — the “static king” of old was finding its form.

Her fate, like her build, was never going to be smooth. Scrutineering came and went quickly. On the dynamic side, the figure-eight and the acceleration both set new bests for the four-motor era. Then came the skidpad — traditionally one of SCUT’s strongest events — and the car’s electrical system chose that moment to misbehave. 64 seconds was her time, and she set it with only the front motors turning. Even so, she still made the top heat of endurance. We all kept hoping — hoping EF26 would tear up the endurance run and finally show the speed she really had.

Another bucket of cold water before endurance. One rear motor simply would not turn; we pulled the gears out of its reduction box. From the moment the green flag fell, she was no longer whole. Xuan brought her home safely, the driver change came and went, and the TSAL light went green.

Nobody saw the red light come on again. Her race was over.

We will never know how fast EF26 could have gone. But all of us know that EF26 was a fast car.

In the 2027 season she becomes A02, taking the mantle from E34, gaining an autonomous system and going on serving the team. We believe her red light will come on again, and her story will go on being written. SCUT Racing: still daring to fight, still striving for perfection.

AF26.story:
A-Future26 is our seventh-generation driverless formula car, twelve months in the making.

Built on E-Future26's body, she carries every mechanical quality a fast car needs — quick and stable. After all the setup experience A-Future25 accumulated, nobody expected her to be hard to drive — including the autonomous system.

Yet last season's shadow still hangs over this car, and over everyone who built her. “Hefei, a year ago. The driverless car DNF'd in the acceleration, then went into a death wobble in the tracking event — that failure followed me around for most of a year. Can the car finish? Is it fast enough? What kind of car, and what kind of team, does it actually take?” That is how Zhao Ziqian — AF25's autonomous-system lead and AF26's driverless team captain — puts it.

Nobody was beaten down by that shadow; we turned it into fuel. No idiom really covers the nights spent on code, but commit after commit on GitHub made this car's eyes brighter, her acceleration stronger, her steering freer. In one year we built our own highly customised simulation platforms — two of them, in fact — and a virtual AF25 ran lap after lap inside them; we built a stable speed planner, a complete SLAM and planning stack, a fast and precise MPC… and none of us thought “that's enough.” Everyone understood one thing: to show 100% on track, you have to put in 150%.

“In the end we got an answer we can live with,” Zhao Ziqian adds. “A04 grew up being pulled along by the whole team, and looked after by seniors from several seasons — he is very lucky. All three events performed to expectation and finished cleanly. Thank you all for putting together such a fine piece of work.”

We finally met a stable, fast, intelligent driverless car; we watched her go from yellow to blue in the high-speed tracking event, and watched her step onto the runner-up's podium.

But more importantly, we proved that we have a team that is proactive, united, meticulous and able to execute. That is a spirit worth far more than any award. And we believe the SCUT driverless team will carry it onward, toward the highest step of the podium.
